Chapter 4 Initial diversity analyses

We use hilldiv3 to describe diversity in the selected panel. Neutral Hill numbers use representative relative abundances; phylogenetic Hill numbers also use the pruned representative tree. We evaluate diversity orders \(q=0\) (all detected units receive full weight), \(q=1\) (abundance-weighted diversity), and \(q=2\) (common units weighted more strongly). For neutral diversity, \(q=0\) is the count of detected representatives. Functional diversity awaits a matched trait or gene-function table.

4.1 Within-sample diversity

ggplot2::ggplot(alpha_diversity,
                ggplot2::aes(x = value, y = habitat)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.55,
                        fill = "#e6c7c7", colour = "#702626") +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter(height = 0.13, width = 0, alpha = 0.28,
                       size = 0.65, colour = "#702626") +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(type, order), ncol = 3,
                      scales = "free_x") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Hill diversity", y = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                 strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"))

Hill numbers for 45 samples in each habitat class. Boxes show medians and interquartile ranges; points are individual samples. Horizontal scales differ by panel.

q1 <- alpha_diversity[alpha_diversity$q == 1, ]
q1_summary <- aggregate(
  value ~ habitat + type, data = q1,
  FUN = function(x) sprintf("%.1f [%.1f–%.1f]",
                            median(x), unname(quantile(x, 0.25)),
                            unname(quantile(x, 0.75)))
)
q1_neutral <- q1_summary[q1_summary$type == "Neutral", c("habitat", "value")]
q1_phylo <- q1_summary[q1_summary$type == "Phylogenetic", c("habitat", "value")]
names(q1_neutral)[2] <- "Neutral q = 1"
names(q1_phylo)[2] <- "Phylogenetic q = 1"
q1_table <- merge(q1_neutral, q1_phylo, by = "habitat", sort = FALSE)
q1_table <- q1_table[match(habitat_levels, q1_table$habitat), ]
names(q1_table)[1] <- "Habitat"
rownames(q1_table) <- NULL
knitr::kable(q1_table, row.names = FALSE)
Habitat Neutral q = 1 Phylogenetic q = 1
Agricultural field soil 47.8 [41.2–58.8] 4.9 [4.5–5.1]
Natural grassland soil 55.1 [38.9–67.3] 4.5 [4.1–5.0]
Natural forest soil 74.5 [47.9–107.0] 4.8 [4.3–5.3]
Urban greenspace soil 48.4 [39.1–64.9] 4.8 [4.4–5.1]
Natural bog/fen soil 52.7 [35.6–67.6] 4.4 [3.8–5.1]
Natural freshwater sediment 50.6 [32.8–73.2] 5.4 [4.3–6.2]
Natural saltwater sediment 48.3 [37.4–65.7] 4.7 [3.9–5.1]
Urban wastewater water 78.0 [66.6–93.6] 7.9 [7.3–8.5]

Median [interquartile range] of \(q=1\) diversity by habitat.

At \(q=1\), median neutral diversity ranges from 47.8 in Agricultural field soil to 78.0 in Urban wastewater water.

The phylogenetic values use hilldiv3’s common pooled reference tree depth, so samples are evaluated on the same scale. Their numerical values should be compared within the phylogenetic panels, rather than interpreted as counts of MAGs. Neutral \(q=0\) is the number of representatives with a positive reported abundance; it is sensitive to very small values in the source profiles.

4.2 Partitioning across habitats

The next calculation partitions diversity across individual samples, habitat classes, and the complete panel. At each step, hilldiv3 reports a beta factor: the effective number of distinct units added at that scale. The two beta factors multiply to give the total gamma-to-alpha ratio. Each sample has equal weight; the design has 45 samples in every habitat class.

habitat_metadata <- data.frame(
  habitat_class = sample_metadata$habitat_class,
  row.names = sample_metadata$sample_id
)
partition_neutral <- plain_hill_result(hilldiv3::hillpart(
  overview_abundance, q = c(0, 1, 2),
  hierarchy = ~ habitat_class, metadata = habitat_metadata,
  type = "neutral"
))
Partitioning neutral Hill numbers across scales "sample < habitat_class <
total".
partition_phylogenetic <- plain_hill_result(hilldiv3::hillpart(
  overview_abundance, q = c(0, 1, 2), tree = genome_tree,
  hierarchy = ~ habitat_class, metadata = habitat_metadata,
  type = "phylogenetic"
))
Partitioning phylogenetic Hill numbers across scales "sample < habitat_class <
total".
partition_neutral$type <- "Neutral"
partition_phylogenetic$type <- "Phylogenetic"
partition <- rbind(partition_neutral, partition_phylogenetic)
stopifnot(all(is.finite(partition$diversity)),
          all(is.finite(partition$beta[partition$scale != "sample"])))

within <- partition[partition$scale == "habitat_class",
                    c("type", "q", "beta")]
between <- partition[partition$scale == "total",
                     c("type", "q", "beta", "diversity")]
names(within)[3] <- "Within habitats"
names(between)[3:4] <- c("Between habitats", "Gamma diversity")
partition_table <- merge(within, between, by = c("type", "q"), sort = FALSE)
partition_table <- partition_table[order(match(partition_table$type,
                                                c("Neutral", "Phylogenetic")),
                                          partition_table$q), ]
knitr::kable(partition_table, digits = 2)
type q Within habitats Between habitats Gamma diversity
Neutral 0 7.50 3.66 3552.00
Neutral 1 5.04 3.33 893.78
Neutral 2 4.80 2.76 334.78
Phylogenetic 0 4.17 3.29 611.03
Phylogenetic 1 1.46 1.56 21.51
Phylogenetic 2 1.12 1.12 6.19

Hierarchical Hill-number partition. Beta factors describe sample-to-habitat and habitat-to-panel turnover; gamma is diversity in the full panel.

At \(q=1\), neutral beta diversity is 5.04 from samples to habitats and 3.33 from habitats to the full panel. The corresponding phylogenetic factors are 1.46 and 1.56.

These are descriptive comparisons of a geographically selected panel. Habitat and collection year are not independently balanced, so these summaries do not by themselves establish habitat effects. Relative abundances also cannot support read-count rarefaction or sampling-depth uncertainty estimates.
